snippet: Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Management, or similar field preferred * 6+ years of refractory experience * Technical knowledge of Caster, Melt Shop, Ladle Metallurgy Facility (LMF), and ... A Refractory Engineer typically spends their day assessing the condition of refractory linings in furnaces or kilns, designing solutions for heat-resistant construction, and coordinating with maintenance and production teams for installation or repair projects. Routine tasks may include inspecting refractory performance, analyzing failure causes, preparing technical reports, and selecting materials that meet thermal and chemical requirements. A refractory engineer designs, selects, and oversees the installation and maintenance of refractory materials used to line high-temperature industrial equipment such as furnaces, kilns, and reactors. They ensure the materials can withstand extreme heat, chemical exposure, and thermal cycling, often using specialized tools and technical knowledge to optimize performance and safety. Work with high-temperature and specialty materials (refractory metals, ceramics, alloys) to meet durability and performance requirements for thermochemical applications · Partner with engineers to interpret technical drawings, troubleshoot fabrication challenges, and recommend design improvements for manufacturability

title: Refractory Manufacturing Roles: The Different Types of Refractory Jobs
snippet: Refractories are materials that have been specifically designed to withstand high temperatures and/or corrosive environments. Refractory jobs involve working with refractory materials and industrial equipment, such as a furnace, broiler, and kiln. There are many different types of refractory roles, each with its own responsibilities and duties. Refractory engineers also work with customers to determine their specific needs and requirements, such as material selection. They must be able to think creatively and come up with innovative solutions that meet the customer's needs while still staying within budget. Refractory technicians: Refractory technicians are responsible for installing, repairing, and maintaining refractory equipment and materials. This includes everything from the installation of new equipment to the repair of damaged components. They must be able to work quickly and efficiently to keep the equipment running smoothly and safely. Refractory technicians must also be able to troubleshoot problems and come up with solutions. This can be a challenging but rewarding role, as it requires a high level of expertise and technical knowledge. Refractory workers: A refractory worker is responsible for loading and unloading refractory materials and performing other manual labor tasks.
